   MINUTES OF TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 28, 2021
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL
  HUMAN EQUITY, ACCESS, AND RELATIONS (HEAR) COMMISSION

CALL TO ORDER

Chair Jennings-Nuñez called the special meeting of the HEAR Commission to order at 6:37 p.m.
on Tuesday September 28, 2021 with all Commissioners and staff participating by
teleconference.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Commissioner Khan.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present:  Jacqueline Borja, Michelle Brenhaug, Susan Fitzsimmons, Viki Goto,
  Jorge Herrera, Riaz (Rick) Khan and Chasity Jennings-Nuñez
Commissioners Absent:  None

ANNOUNCMENTS

Recreation Supervisor Matthew Morales-Stevens provided information for the public on how to
submit comments, and how to request meeting agendas. If you wish to address the HEAR
Commission, e-mail all public comments to mmoralesstevens@sgch.org.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  A motion was made by Chair Jennings-Nuñez, seconded by Commissioner Brenhaug to
  approve the agenda with the reorder of the following discussion items- moving The Land
  Acknowledgement discussion to 4B and moving Discussion of the Annual Workplan and
  Action Plan to 4D.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 7-0-0 as follows:
  Ayes: Borja, Brenhaug, Fitzsimmons, Goto, Khan, Herrera, Jennings-Nuñez
  Nays: None

HEAR COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  SEPTEMBER 28, 2021
   Abstain: None

  2. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Public Comment: Community Services Commissioner, Cheryl Cabot commented about a
  comment that was made during the Commissioner Comment agenda item, during the
  August 26, 2021 HEAR Commission Special Meeting, with respect to the city budget.

  3. ACTION ITEMS

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  A motion was made by Commissioner Goto with an amendment that
  Commissioner Goto volunteered to assist Commissioner Borja on the development
  of the youth survey, seconded by Commissioner Borja to approve the minutes of
  the HEAR Commission Regular Meeting for August 26, 2021.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 7-0-0 as follows:
  Ayes: Borja, Brenhaug, Fitzsimmons, Goto, Khan, Herrera, Jennings-Nuñez
  Nays: None
  Abstain: None

  4. DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A. GUEST SPEAKER- BERT NEWTON- MAKING HOUSING AND COMMUNITY
  HAPPEN

  Mr. Newton spoke on rezoning religious land for affordable housing and related
  local and state initiatives.

  Public Comment: None

  B. LAND ACKNOWLEDGMENT STATEMENT

  Chair Jennings-Nuñez provided an update on the first Land Acknowledgement
  Statement (LAS) Advisory Committee meeting. She stated that Commissioner
  Lubisich from the HPCRC is the advisory committee chair and Commissioner
  Jennings-Nuñez was selected as Vice-Chair.

  Commissioner Brenhaug provided an in-depth update on the items that were
  discussed at the LAS Advisory Committee meeting.

  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Recreation Supervisor, stated that the next LAS
  Advisory Committee meeting will be held on October 6 at 6:30pm and shared what
  will be discussed at the meeting.

HEAR COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  SEPTEMBER 28, 2021
   Public Comment: None

  C. AGENDA TRANSLATION UPDATE

  City Manager, Mark Lazzaretto, explained that the City Council approved the
  translation of the City Council and HEAR Commissions agendas from English into
  Spanish, Chinese and Vietnamese at the September 7, 2021 City Council meeting.

  Public Comment: None

  D. DISCUSSION OF THE ANNUAL WORKPLAN AND ACTION PLAN

  The Annual Workplan was approved with amendments at the June 15 City Council
  meeting. Commissioners discussed progress made on each item. Primary items
  discussed at this meeting included Community Engagement, Youth Engagement
  and Partnerships.

  Chair Jennings updated the Commission on the progress made related to the
  Community Engagement workplan item, including the Native American Heritage
  Month celebration and guest speakers at commission meetings.

  Commissioners Borja and Goto provided a draft of the questions to be included in
  the youth engagement survey. Commissioner Goto mentioned that this could be
  used on a community wide scale. Discussion was had regarding how best to
  disseminate the survey.

  Discussions occurred surrounding the development of a youth liaison application
  and supplemental materials that were included in the agenda packet.

  Chair Jennings-Nuñez asked that the commission bring workplan item 1- Equity
  Training to the forefront of discussion for future meetings and Commissioner
  Fitzsimmons provided an update on the training that the San Gabriel Police
  Department officers are currently receiving related to this topic.

  Vice-Chair Herrera provided an update on a meeting that he had with Jonathan Fu,
  Public Information Officer regarding accessibility, specifically related to
  accessibility of information.

  Public Comment: None

  5. COMMISIONER COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

HEAR COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  SEPTEMBER 28, 2021
   Commissioner Fitzsimmons provided an update on the discussion she had with City Staff
  related to the Draft Historic Context Statement.

  Commissioner Goto shared information from the LA County Youth Commission meeting
  that she attended. She also shared that she attended an exhibit at the American National
  Museum entitled “A Life in Pieces- the Diary and Letters of Stanley Hiyami”. Finally, she
  announced that the Los Angeles Asian Pacific Film Festival is occurring until October 2 and
  is showing a variety of free and fee based films.

  Commissioner Borja attended a webinar on critical race theory by the University of
  Redlands and shared her notes from the meeting. She announced that the University of
  Redlands will host another webinar on ethnic studies on October 27.

  Chair Jennings provided additional notes from the University of Redlands’ webinar on
  critical race theory. She also provided a reminder that it is currently Hispanic Heritage
  Month.

  6. STAFF COMMENTS

  No staff comments.

  7. ADJOURNMENT
  Chair Jennings-Nuñez adjourned the meeting at 8:46 p.m.

  Next regular meeting held on October 26, 2021 via teleconference at 6:30pm.

HEAR COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  SEPTEMBER 28, 2021
   Proclamation
  Native American Heritage Month
WHEREAS, during National Native American Heritage Month, we recognize
that Tovaangar was the name given to the ancestral land on which the City of
San Gabriel and its residents reside today; and
WHEREAS, there is a long history of actions, from the arrival of the Spanish
colonizers to Federal policies that sought to assimilate and displace Native people
and eradicate Native cultures, their culture has survived by the strength and
perseverance of the Kizh/Tongva/Gabrieleño people and is inextricably woven
into the history of this country; and
WHEREAS, the descendants of the Kizh/Tongva/Gabrieleño tribes remain
dedicated to the preservation, practice and advancement of their rich and vibrant
culture, and contribute to the San Gabriel community; and
WHEREAS, during the month of November, we honor our native peoples in this,
their ancestral home, and recognize their continued contributions in strengthening
the diversity of our society.
NOW, THEREFORE, I, Chin Ho Liao, Mayor of the City of San Gabriel,
California on behalf of the City Council, Vice Mayor Tony Ding, Councilmembers
John R. Harrington, Denise Menchaca, and Jason Pu do hereby proclaim
November 2021 as “Native American Heritage Month” in the City of San
Gabriel, and encourage the community to join in this observance.
